title: Payments Fraud Risk Data Platform
summary: A governed fraud-risk validation register that publishes all 1,852,394 allowlisted simulated events for bounded analytical queries while keeping identity-like fields, model scores, and payment actions out of the public system.
outcome: Retain the ordinary logistic baseline for the measured 1% review queue. It reaches 0.160 PR-AUC and 51.3% recall while the class-weighted challenger performs worse on ranking, recall, and probability error.

deployment.provider: Render Free, Vercel Hobby, and Supabase Free
deployment.runtime: Read-only FastAPI service, server-rendered Next.js dashboard, and compact indexed PostgreSQL publication store

metrics: 1,852,394 validated simulated events and matching point-in-time feature rows
1,852,394 publicly queryable rows through seven allowlisted fields
Baseline PR-AUC 0.1599 versus challenger PR-AUC 0.1120 on a 555,719-row chronological holdout
Baseline recall 51.3% at a fixed 1% review rate, representing 5,557 analyst slots
Baseline Brier score 0.0040 versus challenger Brier score 0.0767
286 MB hosted publication database including every public row and supporting index

stages: Validate approved simulated source before governed use
Load events and prior-row features with deterministic PostgreSQL contracts
Compare baseline and challenger on a chronological holdout
Normalize the complete public store within the data boundary
Serve bounded read-only event queries and fixed evidence
Present the decision, capacity, and failure states in Next.js
architecture: Source validation rejects schema drift and null analytical fields
Governed PostgreSQL load builds prior-row history without current-event leakage
Chronological evaluation compares baseline and challenger at fixed capacity
Compact Supabase store retains every allowlisted simulated event
FastAPI enforces cursor pagination and bounded parameterized filters
Next.js register exposes decisions, evidence, queries, and failure states
evaluation: Both policies train on 1,296,675 earlier events and evaluate on 555,719 later events
Six inputs are approved: amount, merchant, category, and three prior-row history features
PR-AUC measures rare-event ranking, recall at 1% measures fixed-capacity coverage, and Brier score measures aggregate probability error
The baseline beats the class-weighted challenger on all three reported measures
One chronological holdout supports the release decision but does not establish stability across populations or time periods
Calibration remains uneven, so model scores are not presented as reliable payment probabilities
operationalTradeoffs: Publishing every simulated row improves auditability but requires bounded pages, indexed filters, and abuse controls.
The compact 286 MB public store fits the current free database tier with measured headroom but has no production capacity guarantee.
The governed 2,266 MB development database remains local because features and lineage fields are outside the public boundary.
The read-only service may cold-start or pause on free infrastructure and has no service-level objective.
The model evidence is a fixed offline comparison, not a live scoring, payment approval, or payment decline system.
disclaimer: This public demonstration uses simulated 2019 to 2020 payment events. It is not a production fraud system, does not score a live payment, and does not make an approval, decline, or other payment decision.

story.recruiterSummary: A fraud-risk analyst can inspect the complete 1,852,394-row simulated event register, filter and page through bounded public records, compare baseline and challenger evidence, and see exactly why the ordinary logistic policy is retained for a fixed 1% review queue.
story.technicalNarrative: The product separates governed development data from public analytical data. Local validation locks the approved source and loads deterministic events into PostgreSQL. Window frames end one row before the current event, creating point-in-time merchant and category history without current-label leakage. Both logistic policies share those inputs and a chronological holdout. Publication then normalizes every event into a compact seven-column store whose read-only role cannot access the wider development tables. FastAPI enforces parameterized filters, cursor pagination, and a 100-row ceiling, while Next.js exposes the decision, event evidence, monitoring, and explicit unavailable states.
scalabilityRoadmap: Add gateway rate limits, connection pooling, request telemetry, and service objectives before materially higher public traffic.
Move batch validation and evaluation into scheduled immutable jobs only after defining freshness, retry, retention, and alert ownership.
Add new chronological windows, confidence intervals, threshold sweeps, and delayed-label monitoring before revisiting the model policy.
Move beyond the free 500 MB database tier only with a new capacity review, cost approval, backup plan, and teardown condition.
story.executiveSummary: The ordinary logistic baseline is the stronger measured review policy. On the 555,719-event later partition it reaches 0.160 PR-AUC, 51.3% recall at a fixed 1% review rate, and a 0.004 Brier score. The class-weighted challenger falls to 0.112 PR-AUC, 45.4% recall, and a 0.077 Brier score. The dashboard makes that disposition auditable against all 1,852,394 allowlisted simulated events without presenting a live payment score or action.
story.intendedUser: A fraud-risk analyst or data-platform reviewer assessing offline model evidence, review capacity, and publication controls.

technologyDecisions.rationale: Historical merchant and category behavior is computed at the event timestamp without using the current event or label.
technologyDecisions.alternative: Precompute features in an unversioned dataframe
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: The SQL contract is explicit and reproducible but the wider governed database remains local.

technologyDecisions.rationale: A later source partition tests the policies against future simulated events and keeps the comparison capacity-aware.
technologyDecisions.alternative: Random split or highest single metric
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: One chronological holdout is more realistic than a random split but does not quantify variance.

technologyDecisions.rationale: Dictionary encoding and integer amounts fit all approved rows plus indexes inside the existing free database tier.
technologyDecisions.alternative: Publish the 2,266 MB governed development schema
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: The compact store removes features and lineage detail from public queries by design.

technologyDecisions.rationale: Stable indexed cursors and a fixed 100-row ceiling keep anonymous full-row access bounded.
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: Visitors query the complete population incrementally rather than downloading it in one response.

limitations: The source is simulated and covers January 2019 through December 2020.
Evidence comes from one chronological holdout without confidence intervals.
The challenger is a class-weighted configuration of the same model family, not a distinct algorithm.
Calibration is uneven, so scores are not reliable payment probabilities.
No fairness analysis, threshold sweep, delayed-label feedback loop, or production drift study is claimed.
No live scoring, approval, decline, or automated payment action exists.
Free-tier services may cold-start, pause, or reach capacity and have no uptime guarantee.

bulletCandidates.bullet: Built a governed PostgreSQL pipeline over 1,852,394 simulated payment events with deterministic ingestion, prior-row-only features, zero duplicate IDs, and a compact seven-column publication store containing every approved row.

Compared ordinary and class-weighted logistic policies on a 555,719-event chronological holdout and retained the baseline after it reached 0.160 PR-AUC, 51.3% recall at 1% capacity, and a 0.004 Brier score.

Shipped a decision-focused validation register with full-row filters, cursor pagination, capacity evidence, aggregate monitoring, and explicit loading, empty, and unavailable states across desktop and mobile.

Published all 1,852,394 allowlisted simulated events on zero-dollar services while excluding raw files, identity-like fields, features, scores, and payment actions through least-privilege database and API controls.

presentation.question: Which measured fraud-risk policy best uses a fixed analyst queue, and can the decision be audited against every approved simulated event?
presentation.answer: Retain the ordinary logistic baseline. It outperforms the class-weighted challenger on ranking, fixed-capacity recall, and probability error, and the complete 1,852,394-row allowlisted register is publicly queryable for audit.
presentation.decisionSupported: Assess an offline fraud-risk review policy and inspect its evidence without making a live payment decision.
presentation.architectureAlt: Approved simulated files flow through validation, deterministic PostgreSQL ingestion, prior-row feature views, chronological model evaluation, a compact public event store, a read-only FastAPI service, and a Next.js validation register.
presentation.evaluationMode: Earlier 1,296,675-row training partition and later 555,719-row chronological holdout at a fixed 1% review rate
presentation.publicationStatus: The full allowlisted event register, fixed model evidence, public API, and analytical dashboard are live on existing zero-dollar services.
presentation.licenseNote: The Sparkov simulated source is listed as CC0 1.0 and is not redistributed from this repository.
presentation.coverAlt: Fraud-risk validation register showing the retained baseline, public event scope, and model evidence
